Availability of Haemodialysis services free of cost for BPL & Economically Weaker Section(EWS) patients

Services are provided in manner that are sensitive to gender
Availability of female attendant/female staff, if a male staff examine, treat or manage a female patient

1.  Ensure availability of female attendants or female staff if male staff are required to examine, treat, or manage female patients.
2.  Implement clear procedures and policies to address gender sensitivity in patient care.
3.  Provide staff training on gender-sensitive care and respectful patient interactions.
Access to facility is provided without any physical barrier & friendly to specially able people
Availability of Wheel chair and stretcher for easy Access to the Dialysis unit

1.  Ensure availability of both a wheelchair and stretcher for easy access to the dialysis unit.
2.  Regularly check and maintain the availability of wheelchairs and stretchers.
3.  Install a ramp with an appropriate gradient (1:8) to ensure smooth access for patients with mobility issues.
4.  Ensure at least one disabled-friendly toilet is readily accessible to the dialysis unit.
5.  Regularly check the condition and accessibility of the toilet for patients with special needs.

Availability of ramp with appropriate gradient

2.  Regularly inspect and maintain the ramp to ensure compliance with accessibility standards.
3.  Display clear signage indicating the ramp’s location for easy identification by patients and visitors.
Access to facility is provided without any physical barrier & friendly to specially able people

2.  Check for proper maintenance of the toilet, including handrails, wide doors, and other accessibility features.
3.  Ensure clear signage for the location of the disabled-friendly toilet.

There is no discrimination on basis of social & economic status of patients.
There is no discrimination on the basis of social and economic status of the patients

1.  Regularly review patient records to ensure there is no discrimination based on social or economic status.
2.  Implement policies to ensure equal treatment for all patients, regardless of background.
3.  Establish a feedback or grievance mechanism for patients to report any form of discrimination.
4.  Conduct routine audits to check for any discrepancies or bias in service delivery.
Adequate visual privacy is provided at every point of care

1. Ensure the availability of screens or curtains between patient beds for visual privacy.
2.  Regularly check the placement and condition of screens/curtains to ensure patient privacy.
3. Train staff to ensure that privacy is maintained during patient care procedures.
Confidentiality of patients records and clinical information is maintained
Patient Records are kept at secure place beyond access to general staff/visitors

1. Ensure that patient records are stored securely, accessible only to authorized personnel.
2. Maintain a separate, locked area for the storage of patient records.
3. Regularly review security protocols for safeguarding clinical information.
4. Implement secure digital systems for maintaining electronic records with restricted access.
The facility ensures the behaviours of staff is dignified and respectful, while delivering the services
Behaviour of staff is empathetic and courteous

1. Ensure that staff behavior is always empathetic and courteous when delivering services.
2. Provide regular staff training on maintaining professional conduct and empathetic patient interactions.
3. Implement a feedback system for patients to report any behavior concerns.
The facility ensures privacy and confidentiality to every patient, especially of those conditions having social stigma, and also safeguards vulnerable groups
Privacy and confidentiality of HIV cases

1. Ensure that HIV patients' records are speacial coded and their status is not displayed publicly.
2. Review internal policies for maintaining the confidentiality of sensitive conditions.
3. Provide training to staff on handling sensitive patient information with discretion and respect.
4.  Safeguard the privacy of patients with social stigma conditions, ensuring confidentiality at all stages of care.
There is established procedures for taking informed consent before treatment and procedures
Informed consent are obtained from the patient/ next of kin/ legal guardian as and when required

1.  Ensure informed consent is obtained from the patient, next of kin, or legal guardian as required before treatment or procedures.
2.  Ensure the consent process includes information on the patient's general condition, treatment options, potential adverse reactions, consequences of missing dialysis, risks, and complications.
3.  Make informed consent a mandatory requirement before each session or procedure, as per the facility protocol.
4. Regularly audit the informed consent process to ensure compliance and accuracy.
Patient is informed about his/her rights and responsibilities.
Patients' rights and responsibilities are displayed

1.  Display clear signage of patients' rights and responsibilities in accessible areas within the dialysis unit.
2.  Conduct regular awareness sessions for patients to understand their rights and responsibilities.
3.  Ensure that patients have access to information regarding their rights throughout their care journey.
Staff are aware of Patients' rights and responsibilities
Staff is aware of patients' rights  and responsibilities

1.  Conduct random checks to verify that staff are aware of patients' rights and responsibilities.
2.  Include regular training sessions to keep staff updated on policies related to patient rights.
3.  Incorporate the review of patient rights and responsibilities in periodic staff assessments.
Information about the treatment is shared with patients or attendants, regularly
Dialysis Unit has a system in place to communicate with patient/ their family member regarding the nature and seriousness of the illness

1.  Ensure a system is in place for the dialysis unit to communicate regularly with patients and their family members regarding the nature and seriousness of the illness.
2.  Regularly ask family members if they have been adequately informed and involved in the treatment plan and progress.
3.  Provide patient education materials to reinforce communication about treatment.
The facility has defined and established grievance redressal system in place

1.  Check the availability and accessibility of the complaint box within the dialysis unit.
2.  Verify when the complaint box was last opened and ensure that it is regularly checked for received complaints.
3.  Review the complaints received and check for documented actions taken in response.
4.  Ensure a system is in place to address complaints in a timely and systematic manner.
The facility has defined and established grievance redressal system in place
Availability of display of process for grievance re addressal and whom to contact is displayed

1. Check for the display of the grievance redressal process in prominent areas within the dialysis unit.
2.  Ensure that the display clearly includes information on the mechanism for grievance redressal and contact details for the relevant person to approach.
3.  Regularly update the grievance redressal display to reflect current protocols and contact information.
4.  Confirm that patients and attendants are aware of the grievance process and know whom to contact in case of an issue.
The facility ensures that drugs prescribed are available at Pharmacy and wards
All Drugs and consumables as per MoU with the private partner/hospital EML are free for BPL/EWS and other notified patients

1.  Check that all drugs and consumables listed in the MoU with the private partner/hospital are provided free for BPL/EWS and other notified patients as per the facility's EML.
2.  Validate the categorization of BPL/EWS and notified patients through proper documentation and verification by the facility in charge.
3.  Ensure that all notified patients are not charged for prescribed drugs and consumables.
4.  Cross-check that the provided drugs and consumables match those mentioned in the MoU and EML.
It is ensured that facilities for the prescribed investigations are available at the facility
Check that  BPL/EWS and other notified patient has not incurred expenditure on diagnostics from outside

1.  Verify that BPL/EWS and other notified patients have not incurred any external diagnostic costs by reviewing their records and billing details.
2.  Ensure that the diagnostics required for these patients are covered within the facility or through partnerships, as per MoU.
3.  Confirm that the diagnostic costs for APL patients are included in the package rate and do not impose additional charges on BPL/EWS patients.
4.  Cross-reference diagnostic records to ensure no charges are levied on BPL/EWS patients for external diagnostics.
The facility provide free of cost treatment to Below poverty line patients without administrative hassles
Dialysis services are free for BPL and other notified patients

1.  Confirm that dialysis services are free for BPL and other notified patients as per the policy, without any hidden costs.
2.  Cross-check with the billing system to ensure that no charges have been levied on BPL or notified patients for dialysis services.
3.  Ensure that patients who qualify for free dialysis services are registered and properly documented as per the scheme.
4.  Regularly audit the records of BPL and other notified patients to ensure compliance with free dialysis services.

APL Patients are charged as per the MoU rates

1.  Verify that APL patients are charged as per the MoU rates and ensure the charges include drugs, consumables, and diagnostics.
2.  Check if the MoU rates are being followed consistently, and cross-check charges with the provided services (drugs, consumables, diagnostics).
3.  Confirm that the charges are applied correctly, and any discrepancies are promptly addressed.

The facility ensure implementation of health insurance schemes as per National /state scheme.
Dialysis sessions of BPL families registered under PMJAY/Equivalent schemes are funded by respective scheme up to its maximum coverage

1.  Check if dialysis sessions for BPL families registered under PMJAY or equivalent schemes are funded appropriately by the respective scheme, up to its maximum coverage limit.
2.  Verify there is no duplication of payment between the Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme and PMJAY or other equivalent schemes.
3.  Cross-check the payment records to ensure the patient’s claim is correctly processed under the respective scheme.
4.  Regularly audit billing and payments to ensure there is no overlap or double payment for dialysis services under multiple schemes.

2. Implement a system to collect document and track performance data regularly for all key indicators.  
3. Train staff on data analysis techniques to identify trends patterns and areas needing improvement.  
4. Create a dashboard or report template to present trends analysis clearly and effectively during reviews.  
5. Use the insights from trend analysis to develop and implement targeted action plans for improving underperforming indicators.
